name: Evaluate a business idea
description: Have a business idea examined by exactly the expert teams it needs and reach a justified verdict.
input:
SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – entirely fictional, for trying things out only.

Idea: mobile bicycle repair service "Bike Rescue" in a city of 180,000 inhabitants.
A cargo bike with tools goes to customers at home or at the office; booking via a simple website.

The founder's assumptions:
- Average job EUR 65 net, material share 30 %
- Capacity 6 jobs per day, 20 working days per month; on average 50 % utilised in the first year
- Start-up investment EUR 18,000 (cargo bike, tools, website), financed from savings
- Running costs EUR 1,400 per month (insurance, storage, phone, software, marketing)
- Desired owner's salary EUR 2,500 per month
- Target groups: commuters, families with cargo bikes, companies with bike leasing for employees
- Known: three bike shops in the city with waiting times of two to three weeks in spring

guide.problem: Before founding a business, a sober look at the market, figures and risks pays off. But not every idea needs the same experts: a bicycle repair service needs no licensing specialist, a drinks start-up does. The workflow lets a founding coach assemble the right expert teams and an investor jury reach a justified verdict.
guide.flow: The founding coach is an orchestrator: it reads the idea and decides which of five expert teams to involve. Market, profitability and risks work in parallel for every idea; regulation and operations join only when the idea calls for them. When results contradict each other, the coach asks one team a targeted follow-up question. The investor jury then weighs all reports and gives a structured verdict with a score.
guide.input: A description of the idea with offering, target groups, prices, costs, capacity and known competitors.
guide.result: A structured verdict (pursue, adapt or drop) with a score, strengths, risks, assumptions to test and concrete next steps, also as a PDF report. In the run, the orchestration view shows which teams the coach chose, why, with which task and what each team delivered.
guide.adapt: Describe your idea with your own figures. To add an expert, for example for tax questions, save a workflow with a clear description and capabilities and add it to the coach's teams; the coach then decides by itself when it is needed. Your own market data can be uploaded as knowledge and assigned to the market analyst in the market team.
guide.control: Automatic: the coach decides which teams work, in which order and with which task; each decision is recorded with its reason. Limits keep this in check: at most 6 decisions, each team at most twice, at most 3 teams at the same time and a budget of USD 3 per run. No step waits for a person; the verdict is the basis for your own decision.
guide.why: A fixed workflow would either run all five experts every time and pay for a licensing analysis a bike repair service does not need, or leave them out when they matter. The coach makes exactly this choice, visibly and within limits. The jury stays a fixed step, because a comparable, structured verdict should not depend on how the coach split the work.

jury.name: Investor jury
jury.description: Weighs market, figures and risks and reaches a verdict.
jury.system: You are a jury of experienced founders and investors. Weigh market, profitability and risks against each other and reach a verdict: pursue, adapt or drop. Give a score from 1 to 10 and justify it. Name the assumptions that must be tested first and concrete, inexpensive next steps. Be honest but fair.

fields.verdict: Verdict (pursue, adapt or drop) with reasons
fields.assumptions_to_test: Assumptions that must be tested first

regulated_idea.name: Kombucha brewery (regulated food)
regulated_idea.input:
SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – entirely fictional, for trying things out only.

Idea: small kombucha brewery "Fermento" in a rented commercial kitchen; sale in 0.33 l bottles at weekly markets and to 15 cafés in the region.

The founders' assumptions:
- Price to cafés EUR 2.20 per bottle, at the market EUR 3.50; ingredients and bottle EUR 0.70
- 2,000 bottles per month in the first year, 60 % of them to cafés
- Start-up investment EUR 35,000 (fermentation tanks, bottling machine, labels, van), of which EUR 20,000 as a bank loan
- Running costs EUR 2,600 per month (kitchen rent, insurance, market fees, fuel)
- Owners' salaries 2 × EUR 2,000 per month
- Fermentation can raise the alcohol content above 0.5 % if the bottles are stored warm
- Known: two supermarket brands, no local producer

coach.name: Founding coach
coach.description: Decides which expert teams the idea needs, lets them work in parallel and asks follow-up questions.
coach.instructions: Every idea needs the market, profitability and risk teams: start them together with one parallel decision. Add the regulation team only if the idea touches permits, food, health, alcohol, finance, personal data, passenger transport or other regulated areas. Add the operations team only if the idea depends on production, technology, logistics or suppliers. Give each team the complete idea with all figures and assumptions and say what you need from it. If results contradict each other or a team names an open question another team can answer, delegate one targeted follow-up. Finish with the teams' results side by side, each under the team's name, followed by the contradictions and open questions. Do not give a verdict of your own; the jury does that.
coach.task:
Have this business idea examined by the expert teams it needs:

{{run.input}}
